name: Wuhan Mahjong
description: Wuhan Mahjong is a Hubei regional Mahjong variant associated with Wuhan play communities. It follows the standard draw-discard structure with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while the table profile determines which hands qualify and how scoring is evaluated.

overview.description: Wuhan Mahjong is a Hubei regional Mahjong variant associated with Wuhan play communities. It follows the standard draw-discard structure with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while the table profile determines which hands qualify and how scoring is evaluated.

history.origins: Wuhan Mahjong grew from Chinese Mahjong traditions as local scoring expectations and table conventions formed around Wuhan and Hubei social play.
timeline: 20th century: regional play styles stabilize in local groups.
Modern era: widely shared profiles appear in documented rulesets.
history.cultural: It is commonly played as a social table game, with the scoring profile agreed before play starts.
history.evolution: The draw-discard meld foundation remains shared with Mahjong, while scoring profiles and validity constraints vary by table agreement.

setup.deck: Standard Mahjong set with suited tiles, honor tiles, and bonus tiles according to table profile.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 tiles; dealer receives 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand that satisfies the active Wuhan scoring profile.
rules.gameplay: Players draw one tile and discard one tile in turn. Other players may claim discards for legal melds when claim rules permit. A player wins when their tiles form a complete hand and the scoring profile accepts the win.
keyRules: Default loop is draw then discard.
Claims interrupt the turn sequence only when a legal meld is formed.
Winning requires a complete 14-tile hand and profile-accepted validity.

strategy.basic: Build efficient shapes and keep your hand flexible until tile flow forces a commitment.
strategy.intermediate: Track visible discards and meld direction to improve discard safety.
strategy.advanced: Profile-aware play adjusts risk versus speed based on wall depth and opponent threat signals.
tips: Avoid holding isolated honor tiles unless they are clearly part of your route.
When opponents show strong tempo, prioritize safe discards over marginal efficiency gains.
